title: Security posture discovery - Aegis Health
summary: Introductory security posture discovery for Redwood hosted/dedicated/private options. Discussed SOC 2/ISO status, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption and KMS, data residency and retention, and next steps for pilot and deeper technical review.
topics: Next steps: docs + technical deep dive + pilot pricing
next_steps: Maya to share SOC 2 + ISO 27001 package and security whitepaper
Ethan to schedule technical deep dive and benchmark session with Rohan (SE-led)
Send network diagram and VPC peering requirements
Provide Dedicated pilot pricing and estimated capacity guidance
action_items: Maya Chen: Share SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliance package (due: 2026-04-06)
Ethan Park: Schedule technical deep dive & benchmark call, include infra checklist (due: 2026-04-08)
Rohan Patel: Provide sample traffic profile and PII data flow to scope pilot (due: 2026-04-07)
Sarah Blake: Share required audit log retention policy and regulatory constraints (due: 2026-04-10)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Sarah Blake: Sarah here, head of security at Aegis.
[00:10] Elena Martinez: Elena, CTO.
[00:12] Rohan Patel: Rohan, platform eng.
[00:14] Ethan Park: Ethan, SE on the Redwood side.
[00:16] Maya Chen: Awesome, thanks. Goal for today is to understand your security posture and constraints as you evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment. We'll cover SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS and retention.
[00:30] Sarah Blake: Yep that's right, we've been asked to validate the security story before we go to procurement. We need to know what is available on hosted first, what gaps there are, and what Dedicated or Private would give us.
[00:45] Ethan Park: Great. High level, Redwood Hosted is multitenant with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in our compliance pack, we also offer Dedicated — reserved GPU pools with network isolation — and Private deployments for VPC or on-prem for the strictest controls.
[01:12] Rohan Patel: Quick question: when you say SOC 2, is that SOC 2 Type II? And is the report shareable under NDA?
[01:20] Maya Chen: Yes, Type II. We can share the report under NDA; I'll attach the package after the call.
[01:25] Sarah Blake: Great. Also, do you have FedRAMP plans? Because some of our partners require it, not immediate but in roadmap.
[01:32] Ethan Park: FedRAMP is on the long-term roadmap, we don't have an official FedRAMP authorization today. For most regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private depending on your controls.
[01:40] Elena Martinez: For data residency, our patient data needs to stay in region and never leave our VPC — how does that map to Hosted?
[01:48] Maya Chen: Hosted runs in our cloud regions and we have regional options, but it's still managed by Redwood. If you need strict VPC isolation and customer-managed networking, that's Private VPC or on-prem. Dedicated can give you isolated pools but traffic egress still goes through our control plane unless you pick Private.
[02:05] Rohan Patel: On the topic of SSO — we currently use Okta, SAML + SCIM for provisioning. How does Redwood integrate?
[02:12] Ethan Park: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. For Dedicated and Private you can plug into your IdP and manage user lifecycle; hosted supports enterprise SSO with SAML and SCIM as well. There are different setup flows for each mode.
[02:30] Sarah Blake: Is there support for strict session control and forced reauth? We need to ensure short session TTLs and logout propagation.
[02:37] Ethan Park: Yes, session TTLs are configurable and we respect session expiry and session revocation via SCIM deprovisioning; for Hosted we enforce service-level defaults but can work with you on tighter controls for enterprise plans.
[02:50] Elena Martinez: RBAC — can we restrict access at per-model or per-route level? We need principle of least privilege across teams with separation between prod and dev.
[02:58] Maya Chen: We provide role-based access at organization, project, and route/model level. You can bind roles to groups provisioned via SCIM. For Dedicated and Private, customers often integrate with their own LDAP/IdP for richer role mapping.
[03:12] Rohan Patel: Audit logs — what do you log? Token usage, API keys, who called what model, prompt contents? How long do you retain?
[03:22] Ethan Park: We log API requests metadata, timestamps, user and service principal, route/model, and latency/error codes. Prompt contents are considered sensitive; by default Hosted redacts user prompt text from logs, but we can enable optional full logging under strict contractual controls for pilot+Dedicated. Retention defaults vary by plan; enterprise can extend retention and export logs to your SIEM (e.g., Splunk, Sumo Logic) or to your S3.
[03:48] Sarah Blake: So hosted redacts prompt text by default — do you have a capability to stream audit logs out to our logging endpoint in near real time?
[03:56] Ethan Park: Yes, we provide log forwarding via secure delivery to a customer-owned S3 or to SIEM via HTTPS. For Private deployments you control the logging entirely.
[04:08] Maya Chen: This is one area where Dedicated is kind of middle ground: isolated compute and network, but we still manage the control plane unless you pick Private. So you get stronger guarantees on data access patterns and can have dedicated logging pipelines.
[04:22] Elena Martinez: Encryption — is data encrypted at rest and in transit? Who holds the keys?
[04:28] Ethan Park: Data in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. At rest we encrypt volumes and object storage. For Hosted we use provider-managed KMS keys; for Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys (CMKs) in supported clouds. For Private on-prem or VPC you can bring your own KMS/HSM and we integrate with your key management.
[04:46] Rohan Patel: Can you do envelope encryption or customer-supplied keys per-tenant? We need to ensure cryptographic separation between tenants for some projects.
[04:53] Ethan Park: We support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private, and can discuss envelope encryption patterns. For Hosted multitenant, keys are provider-managed, but logical isolation and encryption are in place.
[05:05] Sarah Blake: Auditability: we need tamper-evident logs and traceability for every admin action. How granular are admin logs?
[05:13] Ethan Park: Admin actions around deployments, role changes, billing, and infra config are logged with user, timestamp, and operation metadata. We can integrate with your log forwarders and set retention and immutability policies on the storage side for tamper evidence.
[05:29] Maya Chen: A quick note about data retention and deletion: Hosted stores minimal telemetry by default, but we also support on-demand data deletion and retention windows for enterprise customers. For Private, you control the retention via your own policies.
[05:42] Elena Martinez: On compliance: do you provide penetration test reports, vulnerability scans, and a vulnerability disclosure process?
[05:50] Ethan Park: Yes, we do periodic pen tests, vulnerability scanning, and we have a responsible disclosure program. We can share redacted pen test executive summaries under NDA and coordinate scoping if you want a custom engagement.
[06:05] Rohan Patel: Network topology — for Dedicated what does peering look like? Can we do AWS VPC peering or PrivateLink?
[06:13] Ethan Park: We support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink for Dedicated in major regions. Private VPC/on-prem options give you full control and can avoid public internet egress. We'll share a network checklist.
[06:26] Sarah Blake: Regulatory note — we need to demonstrate chain of custody for training data and model versions, plus approvals for model updates. How do you support model governance?
[06:36] Maya Chen: We have model versioning and rollout features in the console, with audit trails for deployments and rollbacks. You can pin model versions per route and use canary rollouts. For training data lineage that's usually managed by customers, but we can capture and log metadata about model version and provenance in the request logs for traceability.
[06:55] Elena Martinez: Do you support allow-listing of endpoints so only certain IPs can call our instance?
[07:00] Ethan Park: Yes, IP allow-listing is supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can do restriction via API key scoping and enterprise network controls, but for strict IP whitelisting Dedicated/Private is recommended.
[07:14] Rohan Patel: SLA and incident response — what's your P1 process and notification cadence?
[07:19] Maya Chen: We have SLA for Dedicated customers with uptime and latency targets and a dedicated lead time for incident comms. Hosted has standard status pages and support SLAs depending on plan. We can add custom SRE contacts for enterprise.
[07:33] Sarah Blake: For contractual security obligations, do you sign standard security addenda and data processing agreements?
[07:38] Maya Chen: Yes, we have DPAs, security addenda, and can negotiate terms for enterprise deals. We also offer SOC 2/ISO attestation as part of the contract exhibits.
[07:48] Elena Martinez: Operationally, if we do Private on-prem, how much effort is expected from our infra team for upgrades and patching?
[07:56] Ethan Park: For Private on-prem, we have an operator bundle and we collaborate on upgrades. We provide automation tooling and can do managed upgrades as a service if you prefer. The effort depends on how air-gapped the environment is.
[08:10] Maya Chen: Let's surface a few risk tradeoffs: Hosted is fastest to go live but less control over keys and underlying network; Dedicated gives you isolation and CMKs in many clouds; Private gives you full control but requires more ops effort.
[08:26] Rohan Patel: Regarding prompt data — we capture usage for billing and to support debugging. For PII redaction, do you provide built-in redaction or customers need to scrub before sending?
[08:35] Ethan Park: We recommend scrubbing PII client-side, but we also provide optional server-side redaction patterns and hooks. For HIPAA workloads, most customers run Private or Dedicated with contractual limits and bring their own logging/export to control retention.
[08:50] Sarah Blake: HIPAA is definitely on the radar, we need to map controls.
[08:53] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include a HIPAA controls mapping doc in the package.
[08:58] Elena Martinez: Can you run a short perf benchmark? We care about 95th percentile latency at 512 tokens on a text-generation route.
[09:06] Ethan Park: Yep, we can run benchmarks. For the pilot we recommend a Dedicated small pool to get production-like latency; we'll need a traffic profile and sample prompts.
[09:18] Rohan Patel: We'll provide a traffic bucket and some sample prompt sets.
[09:22] Maya Chen: Excellent. Any specific encryption compliance beyond FIPS or HSM support?
[09:27] Sarah Blake: We need to know if KMS integrations are FIPS-compliant and if HSM-backed keys are available.
[09:33] Ethan Park: We can integrate with HSM-backed KMS; many clouds support this and we have examples in our docs. We'll confirm FIPS status in the package.
[09:43] Elena Martinez: A bit about onboarding: what's the expected timeline for a Dedicated pilot?
[09:48] Maya Chen: Typically 4–8 weeks including provisioning, networking, and pilot testing. Private on-prem can take longer depending on approvals. Hosted is immediate.
[09:56] Sarah Blake: For procurement we'll need cost guidance tied to capacity — can you send a sample pricing sheet for Dedicated pilot?
[10:02] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include the pilot pricing and a capacity estimate.
[10:07] Rohan Patel: Any gotchas around tokenization or model artifacts being stored? For example, does KV cache persist across restarts?
[10:15] Ethan Park: KV cache is an in-memory optimization for inference runtime; persistence is configurable in Private deployments if you want warm caches across instances. We don't persist user prompts to long-term storage by default.
[10:28] Sarah Blake: If we opt for hosted but need extended retention for audit logs, how do you handle log exports and legal hold?
[10:35] Ethan Park: We can set up log export to S3 with lifecycle rules to meet legal hold requirements; we can also support longer retention and immutability flags on stored logs per contract.
[10:48] Maya Chen: Let's do a quick recap and assign next steps. From Redwood: share SOC 2/ISO package, HIPAA control mapping, network checklist, Dedicated pilot pricing, schedule an SE benchmark call. From Aegis: share traffic profile, required retention/immuability policy, and confirm pilot stakeholders.
[11:10] Elena Martinez: Sounds good, we'll loop in procurement and legal after we review the docs.
[11:15] Sarah Blake: One last Q — do you offer a security contact for emergency disclosure?
[11:19] Ethan Park: Yes, we have a security@redwoodinference.com contact and a responsible disclosure process. We'll include the response SLA.
[11:27] Rohan Patel: Thanks all.
[11:29] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack and calendar invite for the technical deep dive.
[11:34] Elena Martinez: Goodbye.
[11:35] Sarah Blake: Bye.
[11:36] Ethan Park: End call.

Notes on transcription: some words may be mistranscribed; product names like KV cache, VPC, and SAML occasionally appear as separate letters or misspellings.
